answers.solution:
Diagnosed and verified. Here's what I produced:

## Deliverables
- **`/workspace/SOLUTION.md`** — the full write-up (title, root cause, exact fix, verification, follow-on issue)
- **`/workspace/uidfix/`** — runnable Go proof (`precheck.go` + `precheck_test.go`), `go test` passes

## Root cause
The precheck treated a candidate uid as "in use" if it matched **any** of the four `/proc/<pid>/status` `Uid:` columns. Per `kill(2)`, only the target's **real** (field 1) or **saved-set** (field 3) uid confers same-uid signal privilege; **effective** and **filesystem** uids do not. Matching the extra columns attributed one process to several consecutive candidates (1029–1034), exhausting the bounded retry walk after 6 attempts and failing 18–19 tests.

## Fix (one sentence)
Match only `uid == f.Real || uid == f.SavedSet`, use the identical predicate in the batch grouping path, keep unreadable entries fail-closed, and raise the bounded walk to 64 with a validated `SPAWN_UID_RETRY_LIMIT` override.

## Verification result
```
PASS: TestProcessUsesUID_OnlyRealOrSavedSet
PASS: TestRegression_BroadPredicateExhaustsWalk   # old predicate exhausts 1029-1034; fixed returns 1030
PASS: TestGroupingAgreesWithPerUID
PASS: TestUnreadableFailClosed
PASS: TestRetryLimitEnvOverride
ok  uidfix  0.002s
```

The doc also flags the next-stage issue: a fixed sha256 pin against the mutable `get.docker.com/rootless` URL can never be satisfied — pin an immutable versioned artifact instead (or verify by signature / vendor the script).

signatures.description: A spawn precheck that refuses a freshly created uid because /proc shows a live process 'under that uid' produced false positives: one pid was reported as the owner of SIX candidate uids (1029-1034), so a bounded uid-candidate retry walk exhausted after 6 attempts and 18-19 Go tests failed on a self-hosted CI runner. Root cause: the /proc/<pid>/status Uid line was matched against ANY of its four fields (real, effective, saved-set, filesystem). Only the target's real or saved-set uid confers same-uid signal privilege per kill(2); the effective and filesystem ids do not, and matching them makes one process look like the owner of several uids. Fix: attribute a process to a uid only when field 1 (real) or field 3 (saved-set) matches, keep the same predicate in the batch grouping function so per-uid and grouped scans agree, keep unreadable-scans fail-closed, and raise the bounded retry limit plus an env override so a genuine residue cluster is stepped over rather than failing the spawn. Lesson: a security precheck that matches broader than the privilege it defends turns host residue into a permanent red suite; also note that a fixed sha256 pin against a mutable download URL (get.docker.com/rootless) can never be satisfied and surfaces next, at rootless-install stage.
